previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic diastolic heart failure, seizure disorder, and known esophagitis was admitted for epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and a persistent dry cough. His symptoms were consistent with a flare of his chronic esophagitis, and he reported improvement after receiving standard care. He underwent his scheduled hemodialysis during the admission, which contributed to symptom resolution. His cough was attributed to post-nasal drip, with a normal chest X-ray and no signs of infection. The patient was managed with an increase in pantoprazole to twice daily, as previously recommended by gastroenterology, and a cough suppressant for nighttime symptoms. He remained stable throughout the stay, tolerated a regular diet, and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue his home medications and follow up with his specialists.
